ohx1f4:407: The biggest obstacle to AI adoption by small businesses today is not that the technology is not powerful enough, but the mismatch between use cases and user capabilities. Anthropic hit the nail on the head in its announcement: small business owners' AI use "often stops at the chat window" — not because they don't know what AI can do, but because existing tools require users to have the ability to "translate business problems into AI problems," and most small business owners have neither the time nor the technical background for that. Claude for Small Business's answer is "workflow as product": instead of making users design their own prompts, it packages the 15 most time-consuming categories of transactional tasks into skills that can be executed with a single click. Strategically, this overlaps in product design with workflow automation tools like Zapier and Make (Integromat), but the core difference lies in the depth and quality of integration — Claude's workflows are not simple "when X happens, do Y" rules, but multi-step reasoning and execution that understands the business context.
